rv.q: 'The Ferryman' is vast, a play that's formally conventional but has an ambition that's out of this world, a sense that it wants to be about EVERYTHING. And insofar as is realistically possible, it succeeds.
Miss this and you’ve missed a marvel.
The acting is pretty spectacular all round.
Jez Butterworth’s vast, sprawling superbly directed (by Sam Mendes) play really does fall into that rare category – unmissable.
